title: Orientation Ledger Export Artifact v0.1
description: A resolved session, exported with a source recorded against every oriented edge. A standalone artifact: it says its own `kind`. The point of it is the taint: an edge an LLM proposed is LLM-proposed, and so is every edge Meek's rules forced from it — a fact only the session's provenance chain can derive, and one that has to travel with the graph or the disclosure machinery downstream has nothing to disclose. `cause_statements` is that graph in the kernel's own statement form, ready to drop into a program.

session.description: The session this exports, embedded verbatim so `verify_orientation_session` can audit it in place and so every source below can be traced back to the answer that carried it.

data_source.description: The marker put on edges the data established. Required to start with `discovery:` so the query side treats them as learned-from-data; which algorithm learned them is the caller's to say, because this module is algorithm-agnostic and would otherwise be guessing.

edges.description: One entry per oriented edge — the same list as the session's propagation provenance, with a derived `source` added to each.

proposal_edges.description: The subset of `edges` whose source came out `llm_proposal`, sorted. A convenience for the disclosure path, derived from `edges` and therefore checkable against it.

graph_learned_from_data.description: Whether any orientation here rests on the data at all. False for a graph a human or an LLM oriented end to end, which is a different claim about the answer and not a smaller version of the same one.

cause_statements.description: The oriented graph as kernel `cause` statements, each annotated with its source. Ready to drop into a program alongside variable declarations and a query, at which point `data_gap_report` can disclose the LLM-proposed orientations.

rule.description: Echoed from the session's propagation provenance — the same vocabulary, because it is the same fact.

roots.description: The applied constraints this edge rests on. What makes the source below derivable rather than asserted.

source.description: Who this edge is owed to. `llm_proposal` if ANY root came from an LLM — the taint is not diluted by agreement, because an edge is unsafe if any part of what forced it was. `data_source` for a data collider. The answer's own source when every root agrees on one. `orientation_multiple` when trusted roots disagree, which is a real state and not a fallback: the edge is jointly owed and no single source can be argued with.
The same value as the matching entry of `edges`. Carried on the statement because this is the form that travels into a program, where the edge list does not.

predicate.description: The node name. Held to no identifier pattern HERE on purpose: node names arrive as data-frame column names, and whether one is also a legal program predicate is `kernel_ast`'s question at the point these statements actually become a program. Asking it here would turn a name a caller can still rename into an export that cannot be produced.

args.description: The constant subjects the caller asked these atoms to be about. Empty gives predicate-only atoms, which is what a program with a single implicit population wants.
